wm-3-stages-20-x-4-5-triple-big-blue-who.shortDescription: WaterMark certified three-stage whole house water filter — 304 stainless steel, Big Blue 20" × 4.5" housings, 1" BSP. Installed once on your mains supply line, filters every tap in the home.
wm-3-stages-20-x-4-5-triple-big-blue-who.description:
Clean, filtered water from every tap, every shower, every appliance in your home — this is the only whole house water filter system you'll ever need to install. The **Enviro Aqua Premium Three Stage Big Blue Whole House Water Filter System** is **WaterMark certified to AS/NZS 3497**, built from 304 stainless steel, and engineered to handle the full water demand of an Australian family home without any drop in pressure.

This is not a portable bench top unit or a basic inline filter. This is a **permanent, mains-connected whole-home filtration system** that a licensed plumber installs once on your main water supply line — and then every litre of water entering your home is filtered before it reaches a single tap.

## Why This System

### 1. WaterMark Certified — The Only System Your Plumber Can Legally Install

Under the Plumbing Code of Australia, any water filter permanently connected to a mains water line must carry **WaterMark certification**. This system does. A licensed plumber can legally install it on your main supply line, issue a certificate of compliance, and your installation is fully covered. Most cheaper systems sold online are not WaterMark certified — your plumber cannot legally install them on a mains line, and your home insurance may not cover you if they fail.

### 2. Big Blue 20″ × 4.5″ — No Pressure Drop, Longer Cartridge Life

"Big Blue" refers to the 4.5″ diameter filter housings — nearly four times the filter media volume of standard 2.5″ housings. This matters in two critical ways. First, water flows through at up to **75 litres per minute** with no perceptible pressure loss, even when multiple showers, taps, and appliances run simultaneously. Second, the larger volume of filter media means **cartridges last significantly longer** before replacement, reducing your annual running costs. Three 20″ × 4.5″ housings with **1″ BSP brass inlet and outlet ports** — the correct size for Australian mains supply lines — complete the package.

### 3. 304 Stainless Steel Enclosure — Built for Australian Conditions

The 304-grade stainless steel enclosure isn't just about looks — though it does look sharp. It is specifically engineered for Australian outdoor and garage installations. **304 stainless is UV-resistant, salt-air resistant, and corrosion-proof**: the chromium-nickel alloy forms a self-renewing protective layer that resists the coastal humidity, summer heat, and UV exposure that corrode powder-coated steel and degrade plastic components over time. If you're in a coastal or high-humidity location, this matters enormously. It's also tamper-resistant, protects the filter housings from physical damage, and presents cleanly on an external wall or in a visible garage location.

## Three-Stage Filtration — What Each Stage Does

### Stage 1 — Sediment Pre-Filter (5 Micron)

The first stage captures **sediment, rust, sand, silt, and suspended particles** down to 5 microns. This is the workhorse stage — it intercepts the physical debris in your water supply before it can clog the more specialised carbon stages downstream. Protecting the carbon stages from sediment load is what makes a three-stage system significantly more effective and longer-lasting than a two-stage system with carbon alone.

### Stage 2 — Carbon Filtration (Chlorine, Chloramine, Taste & Odour)

The second stage uses a **granular activated carbon (GAC) or catalytic carbon** cartridge to remove chlorine, chloramines, taste, odour, trihalomethanes (THMs), and a broad range of chemical contaminants. **If your water supply uses chloramine** — which includes Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, SA Water, Urban Utilities (Brisbane/SEQ), and Icon Water (Canberra) — specify a **catalytic carbon cartridge** for Stage 2. Standard GAC carbon cannot reliably remove chloramine at whole-house flow rates; catalytic carbon can, and the 20″ × 4.5″ housing provides the contact time needed for it to work effectively.

### Stage 3 — Carbon Block Polish (Fine Contaminants & Heavy Metals)

The third stage uses a **carbon block cartridge** for final polishing — capturing any remaining fine particles, residual chemical contaminants, heavy metals including lead and copper, and cysts. Carbon block's dense structure provides longer contact time and finer filtration than GAC, making it the ideal finishing stage. For households with **PFAS concerns**, a high-grade carbon block in Stage 3 provides meaningful reduction of longer-chain PFAS compounds (PFOS, PFOA) from the whole-home supply.

## Pressure Gauges — Know Exactly When to Change Your Filters

This system includes **pressure gauges** that monitor incoming and outgoing water pressure. As cartridges accumulate contaminants, the pressure differential between inlet and outlet increases — giving you a clear, objective signal that a cartridge change is due. No guessing, no unnecessary early replacement, no waiting until the filters are overloaded. It's a feature that cheaper systems don't include, and over the life of the system it saves you money and ensures your water quality never quietly degrades.

## What's Included

- 3 × Big Blue 20″ × 4.5″ filter housings with 304 stainless steel enclosure & frame
- Stainless steel mounting bracket
- 3 × filter cartridges (sediment + carbon stages)
- Pressure gauges
- Housing removal wrench
- Spare O-rings

## Configure for Your Water Supply

The Big Blue format accepts any standard 20″ × 4.5″ cartridge — widely available from Enviro Aqua. Configure for your water source:

- **Town water with chlorine:** Sediment (5µm) → GAC carbon → Carbon block
- **Town water with chloramine** (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Canberra): Sediment (5µm) → *Catalytic carbon* → Carbon block
- **Rainwater tank:** Sediment (1–5µm) → Carbon block → Sub-micron or UV stage
- **PFAS concerns:** Sediment → Catalytic carbon → High-grade carbon block

Not sure which configuration suits your area? Contact us and we'll recommend the right cartridge set for your water supply.

## WaterMark Certification — What It Means for You

WaterMark certification (AS/NZS 3497), administered by the Australian Building Codes Board (ABCB), confirms this system has been independently tested for structural integrity under Australian mains water pressure, verified to use materials that will not leach contaminants into your drinking water, and assessed for correct fittings and pressure ratings. The manufacturing facility undergoes ongoing annual auditing as a condition of maintaining certification.

For you, this means three things: your licensed plumber can legally install this system and issue a certificate of compliance; your installation is covered under your home insurance; and if anything goes wrong, you have the backing of a certified, audited product. Verify this system on the official [ABCB WaterMark Product Database](https://watermark.abcb.gov.au/).

## Installation

Installed on your main cold water supply line — typically at the point where the mains enters your home, in a garage, under the house, or at the water meter. Installation must be carried out by a **licensed plumber** (required under Australian plumbing law for any mains connection). We recommend asking your plumber to add **isolation valves and a bypass** on either side of the system — this allows you to service the filters without cutting water to the whole house.

Central Coast NSW customers: we offer [professional whole house filter installation by licensed plumbers on the Central Coast](/whole-house-installation-package/).

## Ongoing Maintenance

Replace cartridges every **6–12 months** depending on your water quality and household usage. The pressure gauges take the guesswork out of timing — a rising pressure differential tells you a cartridge change is due before water quality is affected. Big Blue 20″ × 4.5″ cartridges last considerably longer than standard 2.5″ cartridges, keeping annual running costs to approximately **$120–$220 per year**. Replacement cartridges are available directly from Enviro Aqua, shipped Australia-wide.

polypropylene-sediment-water-filter-pp-5.description:
The single 20" × 4.5" Big Blue polypropylene sediment cartridge — the cartridge that goes in Stage 1 of every standard whole-house Big Blue filter system in Australia. If you've got a triple-Big-Blue running on your mains, this is the first cartridge in the line.

## What "Big Blue" Means in Practice

The 20" × 4.5" Big Blue format is the de facto standard for whole-house filtration because of two design facts that work together. First, the **4.5" diameter** gives nearly four times the cross-sectional area of a 2.5" slim cartridge — so water flows through at residential whole-house rates without pressure drop. Second, the **20" height** doubles the media volume of a standard 10" cartridge — so the sediment-holding capacity is large enough to last 6–12 months on Australian town water rather than needing changes every quarter.

This cartridge fits the WaterMark-certified [3-stage Big Blue whole-house system](/wm-3-stages-20-x-4-5-triple-big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-system/) as the Stage 1 sediment, the [twin Big Blue system](/twin-20-x-4-5-big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-sys-bb-2-cartridges-set-plus-bra/), and any third-party 20" × 4.5" Big Blue housing.

coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-ct.shortDescription: Big Blue 20" × 4.5" coconut carbon block (CTO) — 5 micron. The standard whole-house carbon stage for chlorine, taste, and odour reduction at full Australian residential flow rates.
coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-ct.description:
The 20" × 4.5" Big Blue coconut carbon block — the carbon stage that pairs with a 20" × 4.5" sediment pre-filter to handle every drop of water entering an Australian home. This is the cartridge that does the chemistry in a whole-house filter: chlorine, chloramine residue, taste, and odour, removed before water reaches a single tap, shower, or appliance.

## Why Big Blue Diameter Matters for Carbon

Whole-house flow demand is the design challenge for any carbon stage. A modern Australian home running showers, the dishwasher, and the washing machine simultaneously can pull 50–75 litres per minute through the filter line. At those flow rates, contact time between water and carbon is short — and a slim 2.5" cartridge would let chlorine break through to the downstream supply.

The 4.5" Big Blue diameter solves this. **Nearly four times the cross-section of a slim cartridge means proportionally more carbon mass in contact with the water at any moment**, and the radial flow path is longer. The combination keeps chlorine reduction effective at whole-house flow, where slim formats can't.

## Coconut Carbon, Block Format

The carbon source is coconut shell — higher surface area per gram than coal-based activated carbon, with no detectable heavy-metal residuals from the source material. Block construction (rather than granular fill) means longer water-to-carbon contact time at the same flow rate, no media migration into the downstream supply, and predictable pressure drop until end of life.

## Standard Whole-House Spec

This cartridge fits as **Stage 2 carbon** in:

- The WaterMark-certified [3-stage Big Blue whole-house system](/wm-3-stages-20-x-4-5-triple-big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-system/)
- The [twin Big Blue whole-house system](/twin-20-x-4-5-big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-sys-bb-2-cartridges-set-plus-bra/)
- The [premium 3-stage Big Blue system](/premium-three-stage-big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-system/)
- Any third-party 20" × 4.5" Big Blue housing

## A Note on Chloramine

If your water supply uses **chloramine** rather than chlorine — which includes Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, SA Water, Urban Utilities (Brisbane/SEQ), and Icon Water (Canberra) — a standard coconut carbon block may not fully remove chloramine at whole-house flow rates. Catalytic carbon is the better choice for chloramine. Speak to us about your water supply if you're not sure which carbon format fits your area.

- **Micron rating:** 5 micron

- **Lifespan:** 6–12 months

granular-activated-carbon-water-filter-g.shortDescription: Big Blue 20" × 4.5" granular activated carbon (GAC) cartridge — 5 micron, 3–5 month service. The whole-house carbon format where low pressure drop matters more than block contact time.
granular-activated-carbon-water-filter-g.description:
The 20" × 4.5" Big Blue granular activated carbon cartridge — the GAC counterpart to the [Big Blue carbon block](/coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-cto-5-micron-20-x-4-5/). Same housing, same diameter, same drop-in format — different carbon construction, different performance trade-off.

## Why Pick GAC at Big Blue Scale

Whole-house Big Blue is the format where the GAC vs block decision actually has consequences worth weighing. Here's the trade-off in concrete terms:

**Pick this GAC cartridge if:**
- Your installation has marginal mains pressure and you can't afford additional pressure drop across the carbon stage
- You're using this as a Stage 3 polish downstream of a sediment + carbon block in a 3-stage system, where the upstream stages have already done the bulk treatment
- High peak flow events (multiple showers + dishwasher + washing machine simultaneously) need to pass without bottlenecking at the carbon stage

**Pick the carbon block instead if:**
- This is your single carbon stage on chlorinated mains and you want maximum chlorine reduction per cartridge
- Service interval matters more than peak flow capacity — block runs 6–12 months vs GAC's 3–5
- You'd rather not deal with the first-flush carbon-fines flush a fresh GAC cartridge releases

Neither choice is universally correct. Match the cartridge to what your installation actually needs.

## Whole-House Service Interval

At 3–5 months, this cartridge is on a faster replacement cycle than the equivalent block carbon. For whole-house installations with significant flow demand, plan two service visits a year. The shorter interval is the inherent trade-off for the lower pressure drop — granular media exposes more carbon surface to flowing water at any moment, which means the carbon depletes faster.

## Manufacturer Claim and Honest Practice

The manufacturer's documentation lists this cartridge as treating chlorine, hydrogen sulfide, taste, odour — along with broader claims (bacteria, viruses, lead, arsenic, cadmium, iron). The chlorine, hydrogen sulfide, taste, and odour claims are well-established for activated carbon and the cartridge will deliver against those at whole-house flow rates. The microbiological and heavy-metal claims are not established performance for plain GAC media without certified specialised treatment — don't rely on this cartridge as your sole defence against bacteria, viruses, or heavy metals. For those concerns, [UV sterilisation](/big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-and-uv-ultraviolet-sterilization-system/) and reverse osmosis are the established treatments.

commercial-rust-free-filtered-cold-water.shortDescription: Commercial-grade water bubbler in HDPE cabinet with granite-stone finish — WaterMark certified (WMTS-105:2016, licence 23484), lead-free, 20 L/hr cooling at 8–12 °C. For visible outdoor and high-traffic public installations.
commercial-rust-free-filtered-cold-water.description:
A free-standing commercial drinking-water bubbler in a high-density polyethylene (HDPE) cabinet with a **granite-stone finish** — the right look for outdoor courtyards, school grounds, gym entrances, and any visible public-area installation where the standard powder-coated or stainless cabinet would either weather poorly or feel too clinical for the setting.

## WaterMark Certified and Lead-Free

**WaterMark certified under licence 23484** to specification **WMTS-105:2016** — the Australian technical standard for drinking fountains and bubblers. A licensed plumber can install this unit on a mains supply line, issue a certificate of compliance, and the installation is covered under standard insurance. All wetted materials in contact with the drinking water are **lead-free**, which matters for schools, childcare, and any installation subject to ongoing drinking-water lead regulation.

## Why HDPE With a Granite Finish

Standard commercial bubblers come in stainless steel (sharp, modern) or powder-coated steel (cheaper, but rusts at the corners over years). HDPE is neither of those — it's a tough engineering polymer that doesn't rust, doesn't pit at the welds (because there are no welds), and accepts a deep granite-stone texture moulded directly into the cabinet rather than painted on the surface.

For outdoor installations exposed to weather, salt air, or pool chlorine, the HDPE cabinet outlasts powder-coated alternatives. For visual installations — school yards, community parks, park-adjacent gyms — the granite finish reads as 'permanent fixture' rather than 'cheap unit we bolted in'.

## Build and Dimensions

The cabinet stands **122 cm tall** with the bubbler spout rising approximately 7 cm above that (total reach roughly 129 cm to the bubbler nozzle), and a separate side-mounted dispensing tap at about 25 cm above the cabinet top. The 41 cm × 41 cm footprint suits standard concrete pad installation. Internal cooling is a 200 W compressor running R290 refrigerant (60 g charge) delivering 20 L/hr of chilled water at 8–12 °C.

Two-stage filtration — PP sediment plus activated carbon — sits inside the cabinet, accessible for routine cartridge replacement.

## Power and Connection

- 220–240 V AC, 50/60 Hz mains (also runs on 100–127 V 50/60 Hz for export builds)
- Direct mains water connection — no bottles, no jugs, no consumable waste
- Internal drainage routed to a standard waste outlet

stainless-steel-under-counter-drinking-w.description:
An under-counter water chiller that delivers **5 L/hr of chilled drinking water** at 8°C through a dedicated stainless steel tap — installed under the kitchen sink, out of sight, with the tap mounted alongside the existing kitchen mixer or in its own bench hole. The bench stays clear, the chilled water is always available, and the entire assembly is WaterMark certified for legal plumbed-in installation in Australia.

## How It Works

A hermetically sealed 140 W compressor circulates R134a refrigerant through an external copper coil evaporator wrapped around a 2.2 L stainless steel cold tank. The tank holds chilled water at a factory-preset thermostat (adjustable); when you draw water from the tap, fresh feed water enters the tank to be chilled on the next cycle. There's no boiler, no instant-cooling element, no proprietary cartridge — just continuous low-power cooling of a small holding tank.

The **2.2 L cold tank capacity** is right-sized for a household drinking-water tap: it holds roughly six glasses of chilled water on demand and recovers between draws while the rest of the kitchen carries on.

## Build

- **Cabinet:** all SUS304 stainless steel casing — UV-stable, salt-air resistant, won't rust at the welds
- **Cold tank:** 2.2 L capacity in stainless steel
- **Heat exchanger:** external copper coil evaporator insulated with expanded polystyrene
- **Refrigerant:** R134a (55 g charge), hermetically sealed compressor with automatic overload protector
- **Condenser:** wire-tube design with motor-fan cooling — runs quiet enough to install in an occupied kitchen cabinet
- **Refrigerant control:** accurately calibrated capillary tube — no electronic expansion valve to fail
- **Connections:** quick-type 1/4" tubing fittings for inlet and outlet — matches standard under-sink RO and bench-top filter tubing
- **Dimensions:** 41 cm (W) × 21 cm (D) × 29 cm (H)
- **Weight:** 12 kg

## WaterMark Certified for Australian Installation

**WaterMark certified** for plumbed-in installation in Australia. Your licensed plumber can connect this on a mains supply line, issue a certificate of compliance, and the installation is covered under standard home and commercial insurance. Compliance covers the full water pathway — inlet fitting, internal cold tank, and the included stainless steel dispensing tap.

## What It Pairs With

The chiller sits naturally downstream of any filtration system — drop in a [under-sink RO system](/under-sink-water-filter-5-stage-reverse-osmosis-system/) feeding chilled, filtered drinking water at a dedicated tap. The 1/4" fittings are the same format as the Enviro Aqua under-sink and bench-top filter range, so connection is direct without adaptors.

## Service

1 year manufacturer warranty. R134a charge is sealed at the factory; the unit has no consumable parts beyond the upstream filter cartridges if you pair it with a filtration system.

bubbler-filter-cto-plus-pp.description:
An inline replacement cartridge for the bubbler and water-cooler range — combining a polypropylene (PP) sediment stage and a CTO carbon block stage in the standard 10" × 2.5" format used across the line. When the water in your bubbler starts tasting flat, smelling chlorinated, or running off-colour, this is the part you change.

## What Each Stage Does

The **PP sediment stage** is the workhorse: it captures rust, sand, silt, and any particulate that has made it past the home or building's mains filtration. By doing that work first, it stops sediment from prematurely loading the carbon stage downstream, which is what extends overall cartridge life.

The **CTO carbon block stage** then handles the chemistry — chlorine, chloramine residue, taste, and odour. "CTO" stands for chlorine, taste, and odour, which is exactly what carbon block is best at. The dense carbon block structure provides longer water-to-media contact time than granular carbon at the same flow rate, which is why CTO blocks are the standard for point-of-use polishing.

## Compatible Models

Designed for the Enviro Aqua filtered bubbler and cooler range using **10" × 2.5" cartridges**. If your bubbler's housing accepts a 10" × 2.5" cartridge — and the vast majority of residential and small-commercial bubblers do — this is a direct fit.

## When to Replace

For most installations, **every 6–12 months** is the right interval. Heavier-traffic commercial bubblers running through a working day will lean toward 6 months; a quiet residential cooler in a small office can stretch closer to 12. If the water starts tasting like the pre-filter water again — or if flow at the bubbler drops noticeably — change sooner.

Order a spare alongside the cartridge you're installing today; it saves a delivery wait when the next change is due.

drinking-fountain-tap-for-bubbler-cooler.description:
The chrome-plated drinking fountain tap that fits across the bubbler and water-cooler range. When the original bubbler tap on a public drinking fountain has worn out — sticky button, dripping seal, scratched chrome — this is the press-type replacement that fits straight onto the standard 1/4" inlet thread used by most bubbler and cooler designs.

## Press-Type Activation

The tap uses a **press-type valve**: press to dispense, release to stop. Press-type taps are the standard for high-traffic public drinking fountains because they have no levers to break, no sensors to mis-fire, and no exposed cartridge to seize. The mechanism is mechanically simple and rated for the cycling that a school, office, or gym fountain takes through a working day.

## Adjustable Flow Rate

Flow rate is **adjustable** at the tap itself — useful when a fountain is plumbed into a higher-pressure mains line and would otherwise spray rather than arc cleanly. The adjustment lets you tune the drinking-arc to the cabinet height of the bubbler it's fitted to.

## Fitting and Finish

**Inlet:** 1/4" male thread — the standard size used across the bubbler and cooler range. **Finish:** chrome-plated for corrosion resistance and easy cleaning. Wipes down with a standard food-service-safe cleaner.

## Suitable Applications

Replacement or addition for any water cooler, bubbler, or drinking fountain using a 1/4" male-threaded tap fitting. Confirm the existing tap thread before ordering — most units in this category use 1/4" but a small number of older or imported designs use other sizes.

The cooler delivers:

- **Hot:** ≥ 90 °C output at 5 L/hr — sufficient for steady tea and coffee service through a working day
- **Cold:** ≤ 10 °C output at 2–3 L/hr — chilled drinking water on demand
- **Ambient:** room-temperature unfiltered tap for general use

The **safety lock on the hot tap** is a non-negotiable feature for any installation with kids or aged-care residents — the tap won't dispense hot water until the lock is released.

## Working Environment

Designed to run reliably between **10 °C and 32 °C ambient** — covers the full range of a typical Australian indoor environment year-round, including unconditioned laundries and garages in milder climates. Finished in gloss black and white, the cabinet suits both residential kitchens and small office break rooms.

6-stage-reverse-osmosis-water-filters-se.shortDescription: Complete 6-stage RO replacement set with 75 GPD membrane and alkaline cartridge — covers every consumable in a 6-stage under-sink RO system in one order.
6-stage-reverse-osmosis-water-filters-se.description:
A complete 6-stage RO replacement set: sediment + carbon stages + a 75 GPD reverse osmosis membrane + the alkaline post-stage that re-mineralises the permeate water. One SKU covers everything that needs replacing in a 6-stage RO system on its full service interval.

## What's in the Set

Per the manufacturer's parts breakdown:

- **1 × Sediment filter, 10" × 2.5"** — PP sediment pre-filter
- **1 × Granular activated carbon (GAC) filter, 10" × 2.5"** — chlorine and organics reduction; protects the RO membrane downstream
- **1 × Activated carbon block filter, 10" × 2.5"** — secondary chlorine and chemical polishing
- **1 × GAC in-line post-membrane filter** — taste polishing on the permeate side
- **1 × 75 GPD RO membrane** — the purification stage
- **1 × Alkaline cartridge** — re-mineralises and balances pH after RO, putting beneficial minerals back into the water that the RO process strips out

## Why a 6-Stage System Adds the Alkaline Stage

Reverse osmosis is highly effective at removing dissolved contaminants — but it removes beneficial minerals along with the bad. RO permeate water has a low TDS reading and a slightly acidic pH, which some people find tastes "flat". The alkaline cartridge re-introduces calcium, magnesium, and other minerals back into the water and lifts the pH back toward neutral. The result is RO-purified water with the mineral profile and taste of natural spring water.

## Service Interval

Replace the cartridge stages every 6–12 months on typical Australian town water; the membrane every ~24 months. The carbon stages are the most service-critical — if they saturate, chlorine breakthrough damages the membrane irreversibly. Keep the carbons fresh and the membrane will reach its rated lifespan.

Fits any standard 6-stage under-sink RO system using 10" × 2.5" cartridges and a standard 10" × 2.5" RO membrane element.

5-x-premium-quality-cto-carbon-cartridge.description:
A five-pack of premium coconut activated carbon block (CTO) cartridges in the standard 10" × 2.5" format. Five cartridges in one order is the right buy when the cost of *not having a spare on the shelf* outweighs the upfront outlay — facilities managers running multiple under-sink or RO systems, plumbers servicing recurring customers, and property managers with several rentals all share that math.

## When the Five-Pack Makes Sense

A single household with one 2-stage under-sink filter changes the carbon stage roughly once a year. Five cartridges = five years of supply on the shelf, which is more than the carbon stays optimally adsorbent in storage. So the five-pack is **not** the right buy for a single home install.

Where it earns its place:

- **Property managers** with five or more rental properties on a shared service schedule
- **Plumbers and trade buyers** stocking truck inventory for callouts
- **Café, salon, or office portfolio managers** running multiple point-of-use filters
- **RO system owners** changing the Stage 2 carbon at every membrane service (faster cycle than under-sink)

## What's in Each Cartridge

Each unit is a coconut-shell activated carbon block sized to fit any standard 10" × 2.5" filter housing. Coconut carbon is the higher-grade source media — more surface area per gram than coal-based carbon, no detectable heavy-metal residuals from the source material. Block construction (rather than granular fill) gives extended water-to-carbon contact time at residential flow rates, which is what makes the carbon effective for chlorine, taste, and odour reduction.

The cartridges are a direct fit for any 10" × 2.5" housing — same physical size as the [single-pack premium CTO cartridge](/coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-cto-5-micron-10-x-2-5/). Storage tip: keep unused cartridges in their sealed packaging, in a cool dry cupboard, away from solvents or strong odours — activated carbon is adsorbent in storage too, and will pick up volatile compounds from the surrounding air.

coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-ct.shortDescription: Coconut activated carbon block (CTO) cartridge — 10" × 2.5", 5 micron. Reduces chlorine, chemical taste, and odour. Rated 14.5–58 PSI / 5–40 °C.
coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-ct.description:
The coconut activated carbon block cartridge in the standard 10" × 2.5" format — the carbon stage that goes downstream of a sediment pre-filter in nearly every multi-stage residential filter. Where the sediment cartridge handles particulate, this cartridge handles the chemistry: **chlorine, chloramine residue, taste, and odour** are all reduced by adsorption onto the carbon block.

## Block, Not Granular — What It Means in Practice

"CTO" stands for **Chlorine, Taste, Odour** — the three things a carbon block does best. The distinction between this carbon block format and a granular-fill GAC cartridge is mechanical: the carbon here is bonded into a single dense block rather than packed as loose granules. Three consequences follow:

- **Longer water-to-carbon contact time** at the same flow rate — water threads through the dense block rather than channelling between granules
- **No carbon migration** — a block can't shed media into the downstream supply
- **Predictable pressure drop** until the cartridge reaches end of life

For most residential drinking-water applications, block is the right format. Granular still has uses (whole-house high-flow installations where contact time is less critical) but block is the default for under-sink and RO point-of-use.

## Coconut-Shell Carbon

The activated carbon source is coconut shell — the higher-grade source media for water filtration. Coconut activated carbon has more surface area per gram than coal-based carbons (typically 1100–1500 m²/g vs 800–1000 for coal), and avoids the heavy-metal residuals that some coal sources carry. The result is more effective chlorine and taste reduction per gram of media, and a cleaner finished water.

## Operating Window

- **Operating temperature:** 5–40 °C
- **Operating pressure:** 0.1–0.4 MPa (14.5–58 PSI)
- **Lifespan:** 6–12 months depending on water quality and household usage

## Where It Fits

Direct fit for any 10" × 2.5" filter housing — the most common size in Australian residential filtration. Standard pairing: install behind a [10" × 2.5" PP sediment cartridge](/polypropylene-sediment-water-filter-pp-5-micron-10-x-2-5/) as Stage 2 of a 2-stage under-sink filter, or as Stage 2 in any 5- or 6-stage RO system.

coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-ct.description:
The 10" × 4.5" short Big Blue coconut carbon block — same height as a standard residential cartridge but at the wider 4.5" Big Blue diameter. The diameter is what matters here: at nearly four times the cross-sectional area of a 10" × 2.5" cartridge, this format carries significantly more carbon media in the same height, with correspondingly higher flow capacity and longer service life on the same water supply.

## Why This Format Exists

Full-height 20" × 4.5" Big Blue is the mainstream whole-house format. The short Big Blue version is the right answer when:

- The housing cupboard or wall location doesn't have headroom for a 20" cartridge
- The installation is point-of-use rather than whole-house, but the higher Big Blue flow is still wanted
- A caravan, RV, or compact rural setup is using Big Blue housings for ruggedness rather than for whole-house volume

It fits the [10" × 4.5" carbon whole-house housing](/whole-house-water-filter-1-stage-10-x-4-5-carbon/) directly, and the carbon stage of any [2-stage 10" × 4.5" sediment + carbon system](/whole-house-water-filter-2-stage-10-x-4-5-sediment-carbon/).

## What the Carbon Does

**Chlorine, chemical taste, and odour reduction** through adsorption onto coconut-shell activated carbon, bonded into a dense block. ## Why More Media Length Helps Carbon

A carbon stage's effectiveness depends on **contact time** — the duration each parcel of water spends in contact with the activated carbon. At a given flow rate, a taller cartridge means water spends longer threading through the carbon block before reaching the outlet. Two consequences:

1. **Better chlorine reduction at high flow** — a 20" cartridge can hold its chlorine-removal performance at flow rates where a 10" cartridge starts to break through

granular-activated-carbon-water-filter-g.description:
Granular activated carbon (GAC) in the standard 10" × 2.5" format — the alternative carbon format to a CTO carbon block. Where a block packs activated carbon into a dense bonded structure, a GAC cartridge fills the cartridge body with **loose carbon granules**. The mechanical difference drives a different performance trade-off, and choosing between the two is the technical decision that matters for this cartridge.

## GAC vs Carbon Block — The Real Difference

- **Pressure drop:** GAC is significantly lower-resistance than carbon block. Water threads between granules instead of through dense block media.
- **Contact time:** GAC offers **less** contact time per unit length than block, because water can channel between granules rather than being forced through the full media path.
- **Surface area exposed:** loose granules expose more external surface area per gram than a bonded block does.
- **Service life:** GAC saturates faster than block at the same usage level — the WP source rates this format at **3–5 months** vs 6–12 for block.
- **Media migration:** loose granules can shed fines into the downstream supply, particularly during the first flush.

## When to Pick GAC Over Block

**GAC is the right choice when contact time isn't the bottleneck** — typically high-flow applications where pressure drop across a block would be unacceptable, or post-filter polish stages downstream of an RO membrane where the water is already largely treated. **Block is the right choice for residential drinking water at standard flow rates** — the longer contact time delivers better chlorine and taste reduction per cartridge.

For most Australian household under-sink installations, a coconut [carbon block (CTO)](/coconut-activated-carbon-water-filter-cto-5-micron-10-x-2-5/) is the better technical pick. GAC has a clear place in higher-flow whole-house Stage 2 or 3 polish, and as a low-cost taste-improvement cartridge.

## Manufacturer Claims and What They Mean

The manufacturer's specification for this cartridge lists removal of "bacteria, viruses, hydrogen sulfide, chlorine, lead, arsenic, cadmium" and reduction of iron concentration. We present this as the supplier's stated specification. In practice, GAC is **well-established** for chlorine, hydrogen sulfide, taste, odour, and many volatile organic compounds, where adsorption onto activated carbon is the proven mechanism. **Bacteria and virus removal by plain GAC is not an established performance claim** without separate certified bacteriostatic media (typically silver-impregnated). **Heavy metal removal (lead, arsenic, cadmium) by plain GAC has limited capacity** — specialised media or reverse osmosis are the established treatments for these contaminants. If your concern is microbiology or heavy metals specifically, contact us about the appropriate cartridge or system.

A 10" × 2.5" GAC cartridge holds a fixed mass of granular carbon. The 20" version holds roughly double, in the same housing diameter. Three things follow:

A reusable 100 micron sediment strainer cartridge — a washable filter sized for the very dirty end of the water-source spectrum, where finer disposable cartridges would saturate within days and end up costing more in replacements than the original installation. **Tank water, dam water, bore water, rainwater catchment, fish tanks, and any source that has visible particulate going into it** — this is the format that handles those upstream of the actual filtration.

## What 100 Micron Means in Practice

100 micron is a coarse rating by drinking-water standards — about the diameter of a thick human hair. It's deliberately coarse: the strainer's job is to catch the visible chunks (leaves, sand, algae fronds, insect parts, large rust flakes) before they reach the finer cartridges downstream, not to polish water for drinking. A 5 micron sediment cartridge installed first on dam water would clog within hours; the 100 micron strainer takes that load instead, then the 5 micron sediment goes second and lasts as designed.

## Washable, Not Disposable

The key feature that distinguishes this from a disposable PP sediment cartridge: when the strainer reaches its capacity, you unscrew the housing, **rinse the cartridge under a hose, and reinstall**. No replacement cost, no shipping wait. The screw-off end caps make access for cleaning straightforward.

For a tank-water system on a small property, the running cost of this strainer over a year is essentially zero — just the original purchase. Compared to changing disposable PP cartridges every 6–8 weeks at the same sediment load, the savings build quickly.

washable-and-reusable-water-filter-pleat.description:
A reusable pleated sediment cartridge in 10" × 4.5" short Big Blue format — the format that suits whole-house and high-flow installations where a slim 10" × 2.5" cartridge can't move enough water at the system's flow rate.

The key feature is **washable construction**: when the cartridge reaches its dirt-loaded threshold and pressure drop rises, the cartridge comes out of the housing, gets rinsed clean, and goes back in. No new cartridge to order, no service interruption, no waste to landfill. Over the long-term life of the cartridge — typically several years before the pleated media itself wears out — the running cost compares favourably to repeatedly buying disposable PP cartridges over the same period.

## Pleated vs Spun PP

The pleated construction is what distinguishes this format from a standard polypropylene spun cartridge. Pleated media accordion-folds a sheet of filter material into a high-surface-area structure inside the cartridge body. Three differences in practice:

- **Higher surface area** in the same housing volume — more dirt-holding capacity per cartridge
- **Washable** — the rigid pleated structure holds up to rinsing, where loose-spun PP fibres compress and lose their micron rating after washing
- **Longer overall service life** — typically several wash cycles before the media itself reaches end of life

- **Micron rating:** 5 micron
- **Type:** pleated, washable
- **Lifespan:** 6–12 months between washes depending on water quality and usage; multi-year overall service life with proper washing

inline-uf-ultrafiltration-filter-cartrid.shortDescription: Inline ultrafiltration (UF) cartridge — hollow-fibre membrane filtration to 0.01 micron, removes bacteria, cysts, and fine particulate. No waste-water like RO; suits tank water and microbiological-reduction applications.
inline-uf-ultrafiltration-filter-cartrid.description:
An inline ultrafiltration (UF) cartridge — a hollow-fibre membrane filter that physically separates bacteria, cysts, and fine particulate from the water by forcing it through pores measured at the molecular scale. Where reverse osmosis goes finer (down to dissolved ions) and produces waste water in the process, ultrafiltration sits one step coarser and produces no waste — every drop in becomes a drop out, just with the microbes and particulate trapped on the upstream side of the membrane.

## What UF Removes — and What It Doesn't

UF membranes filter at approximately **0.01 micron**. At that pore size, the cartridge captures:

- **Bacteria** (typical size 0.5–5 micron — well above the membrane pore size)
- **Protozoan cysts** including Giardia and Cryptosporidium
- **Suspended particulate** including fine sediment, organic matter, and turbidity
- **Most viruses** in the larger size range, though some smaller viruses (~0.02 micron) can pass through

UF does **not** remove dissolved contaminants — chlorine, fluoride, dissolved metals, and other ionic species pass through the membrane. Pair UF with a carbon stage upstream for chlorine and taste, or with reverse osmosis if dissolved-solid reduction matters.

## When UF Makes Sense vs RO

- **Tank water and rainwater systems:** UF for microbiological reduction without losing 50%+ of the water to RO reject. Pair with a sediment pre-filter and carbon for taste.
- **Town water with microbiological concerns** (boil-water alerts, contamination events): UF as a polish stage adds a physical barrier against pathogens.
- **Anywhere RO is overkill:** UF is simpler, has no waste line, no pump or pressure tank, and runs on standard mains pressure.

## Compatible Systems

Inline format — connects directly into a 1/4" tubing run on a multi-stage filter or RO system. Typically installed as a polish stage in 6-stage and 7-stage filtration setups, or as a standalone microbiological barrier in a tank-water system after sediment and carbon pre-filtration.

inline-water-filter-alkaline-ph-neutrali.shortDescription: Inline alkaline pH-balancing cartridge — 10" × 2", re-mineralises RO permeate water and lifts pH. The post-RO stage that turns flat-tasting purified water into mineral-balanced drinking water.
inline-water-filter-alkaline-ph-neutrali.description:
An inline alkaline cartridge sized for 10" × 2" housings — the cartridge that goes after the RO membrane in a 6-stage or 7-stage RO system to put minerals back into the water and balance the slightly acidic pH of straight RO output.

## Why Alkaline After RO

Reverse osmosis is highly effective at removing dissolved contaminants, but the process strips out beneficial minerals (calcium, magnesium, potassium) along with the bad stuff. Pure RO permeate has very low TDS, slightly acidic pH (typically 5.5–6.5), and a flat taste many people describe as "missing something". The alkaline cartridge solves three problems with one stage:

1. **Re-mineralisation:** the cartridge media releases small amounts of calcium and magnesium back into the water as it passes through
2. **pH adjustment:** lifts the pH from slightly acidic up toward neutral or slightly alkaline (typically pH 7.5–8.5 depending on flow rate)
3. **Taste improvement:** mineral content gives the water the natural mouthfeel of spring water rather than the flat taste of pure RO

## Where It Fits

Installed as the **final stage** of a 6-stage RO system, downstream of the post-carbon stage. The water enters the alkaline cartridge after every other purification step is complete, so what's added at this stage is what reaches the tap.

## Specifications

- **Cartridge size:** 10" × 2"
- **Format:** inline
- **Connection:** 1/4" tube
- **Micron rating:** 5 micron
- **Maximum flow rate:** 0.5 GPM
- **Operating pressure:** 35–80 PSI (241–551 kPa)
- **Operating temperature:** 5–45 °C

inline-water-filter-fluoride-removal-10-.shortDescription: Inline fluoride-removal cartridge — 10" × 2", activated alumina media. The specialised stage that targets fluoride specifically; carbon and sediment cartridges don't reduce fluoride.
inline-water-filter-fluoride-removal-10-.description:
An inline fluoride-removal cartridge using **activated alumina** media — the specialised cartridge that targets fluoride specifically. This matters because the standard cartridges in a multi-stage filter (sediment, carbon, even RO membranes to some degree) don't reliably remove fluoride. If fluoride reduction is what you're trying to achieve, this is the cartridge that does the work.

## Why Activated Alumina

Activated alumina (aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃) is a porous ceramic media with a very high surface area per gram, and it has a specific affinity for fluoride ions in water. As water passes through the media bed, fluoride is adsorbed onto the alumina surface and held there until the cartridge reaches saturation. This is the established water-treatment method for fluoride removal at point-of-use scale — the same mechanism used in larger municipal-scale fluoride treatment plants, scaled down to a residential cartridge.

Activated alumina also captures some other contaminants in passing — chlorine residue and certain heavy metals — but its primary role and design optimisation is fluoride.

## Where It Fits

Inline format with **1/4" tubing connections** — sized for installation as a polish stage downstream of carbon and sediment pre-filters. Typical installation: sediment → carbon → fluoride cartridge → tap. Putting it after carbon matters: residual chlorine reaching the alumina media reduces its fluoride-adsorption capacity.

## Service Life

The cartridge has a rated service life of approximately **1500 gallons (5680 L) or 12 months**, whichever comes first. After that, the alumina media saturates and fluoride breakthrough begins. Replacement is the only option — activated alumina cannot be regenerated at home.

## Specifications

- **Cartridge size:** 10" × 2"
- **Format:** inline
- **Connection:** 1/4" tube
- **Service life:** 1500 gallons or 1 year
- **Operating temperature:** 5–45 °C
- **Media:** activated alumina

inline-water-filter-t33-activated-post-c.description:
An inline T33 post-carbon cartridge — the final polish stage in a multi-stage RO system. "T33" describes the standard inline post-carbon format used across the residential RO industry: a small inline cartridge with activated carbon media, sized for installation downstream of the RO storage tank, just before the tap.

## Why a Post-Carbon Stage Exists

A 5-stage or 6-stage RO system produces purified water at the membrane and stores it in a pressure tank below the sink, ready to be drawn at the tap. But water sitting in a plastic storage tank for hours can pick up faint plastic-tasting compounds from the tank lining, even with food-grade tank materials. The T33 post-carbon stage sits between the storage tank and the tap, removing those storage-related taste artefacts at the moment the water is dispensed. The result is consistently clean-tasting RO water at the tap, regardless of how long the tank has been sitting.

## Specifications

- **Media:** activated carbon
- **Micron rating:** 5 micron
- **Format:** inline
- **Connection:** 1/4" tube
- **Maximum flow rate:** 0.5 GPM

- **Service life:** 1500 gallons (5680 L) or 12 months

## Where It Fits

Replace at every annual service — the post-carbon stage is one of the easier ones to overlook because it sits hidden after the storage tank, but a saturated post-carbon shows up in the tap water as a return of plastic-tank taste.

2-pics-75gpd-reverse-osmosis-membrane-me.shortDescription: Twin pack of 75 GPD reverse osmosis membranes — 280 L/day each, 10" × 2.5" element, rated 55–100 PSI / 4–52 °C. Two membranes covers ~4 years of RO service at the standard 24-month change interval.
2-pics-75gpd-reverse-osmosis-membrane-me.description:
A twin pack of 75 GPD reverse osmosis (RO) membranes — the semi-permeable thin-film composite (TFC) elements that do the actual purification work in a multi-stage RO drinking-water system. The membrane is what separates an RO system from a regular carbon filter: water is forced through molecular-sized pores at pressure, leaving dissolved solids, fluoride, heavy metals, and most chemical contaminants behind on the reject side and producing high-purity permeate on the other.

## Why a Twin Pack

RO membrane lifespan is the longest of any cartridge in the system — typically **24 months** under normal Australian town water conditions, where pre-filter sediment and carbon stages protect the membrane from the things that would otherwise destroy it. Twin pack = one for the next change-out, one for the change after that. Roughly four years of RO service in a single order, at the per-membrane price drop of buying in pairs.

## Performance

- **Production rate:** 75 GPD = 280 L/day
- **Standard rejection:** TFC membranes of this class typically reduce up to 99% of total dissolved solids (TDS) under their rated test conditions, with progressive decline over the cartridge's lifespan

Real-world performance depends heavily on feed water TDS, temperature, and pressure. Cold-water-fed systems on tank water at low mains pressure will produce less per day than the rated 280 L; warm-feed systems on properly pressurised mains can hit the rated figure.

## Operating Window — Read This Before Installing

- **Element size:** 10" × 2.5" (standard RO membrane format)
- **Operating pressure:** 55–100 PSI
- **Operating temperature:** 4–52 °C
- **Critical — chlorine intolerance:** RO membranes of this class are **destroyed by free chlorine**. Every RO system must have a functioning activated carbon stage upstream of the membrane to remove residual chlorine from the feed water. If your carbon cartridge is past its replacement interval, change it before fitting the new membrane — a fresh membrane installed downstream of a saturated carbon stage will fail in weeks rather than years.

## Where It Fits

Direct replacement for any standard 10" × 2.5" RO membrane housing — the format used in the [4-stage](/under-sink-water-filter-4-stage-reverse-osmosis-system/), [5-stage](/under-sink-water-filter-5-stage-reverse-osmosis-system/), and [6-stage under-sink RO systems](/under-sink-water-filter-6-stage-reverse-osmosis-system/), and most third-party residential RO units sold in Australia.

If you also need replacement pre-filter cartridges (sediment + carbon stages) at the same service, the [5-stage RO replacement set](/5-stage-reverse-osmosis-ro-full-replacement-set-with-75-gpd-membrane-nsf/) is the better order — it bundles the cartridges and a single 75 GPD membrane at lower combined cost.

5-stage-reverse-osmosis-ro-full-replacem.shortDescription: Complete 5-stage RO replacement set — 4 cartridges plus one 75 GPD RO membrane, all 10" format. The single order that covers a full annual service on any standard 5-stage under-sink RO system.
5-stage-reverse-osmosis-ro-full-replacem.description:
The complete replacement set for a standard 5-stage reverse osmosis under-sink system — four pre-filter and post-filter cartridges plus one 75 GPD RO membrane, all in the 10" format used by the great majority of residential RO units sold in Australia. One order, one delivery, one service visit covers everything that needs replacing on an annual to biennial schedule.

## What's in the Set

A 5-stage RO system replaces these components on this schedule:

- **Stage 1 — Sediment pre-filter (PP, 1–5 micron):** captures sand, dirt, rust before they reach downstream stages. Replace every 6 months.
- **Stage 2 — Granular activated carbon (GAC):** removes free chlorine from the feed water. **Critical for protecting the RO membrane downstream** — chlorine destroys TFC membranes in weeks. Replace every 6 months.
- **Stage 3 — Carbon block (CTO):** secondary chlorine and chemical reduction; polishes the feed before it reaches the membrane. Replace every 6 months.
- **Stage 4 — RO membrane (75 GPD TFC):** the actual purification stage — reduces dissolved solids, fluoride, heavy metals, and most chemical contaminants. Replace every ~24 months.
- **Stage 5 — In-line post-carbon (T33):** final polish on the permeate before it reaches the tap, removing any residual taste from the storage tank. Replace every 12 months.

## Why Buy the Set Rather Than Individual Cartridges

Two reasons:

1. **Combined pricing:** the bundle drops below the sum of individual cartridge prices, particularly for the membrane.
2. **Scheduling sanity:** the membrane lasts 4× longer than the pre-filters, but it's faster on a single service visit to replace everything together than to track separate change schedules per cartridge. Most RO owners run two service intervals per year: at the 6-month mark, replace just the three carbon/sediment pre-filters; at the 12-month mark, replace pre-filters + post-carbon. This set covers the longer service that includes the membrane every second year.

## Compatible Systems

Direct fit for any standard 5-stage under-sink RO system using 10" cartridges and a 10" × 2.5" RO membrane element — including our [5-stage RO with 3-way tap](/5-stage-undersink-home-drinking-ro-water-filter-system-with-3-way-tap/), the [5-stage RO with stainless tap](/5-stages-ro-system-stainless-steel-tap/), and the great majority of third-party residential 5-stage RO systems sold in Australia.

## A Note on Membrane Replacement Timing

The RO membrane in this set has a typical service life of around 24 months under normal Australian town water conditions, where the upstream carbon stages stay current and the feed water is reasonable quality. If you've let the carbon pre-filters run past their 6-month replacement, the membrane in this set may need replacing sooner than expected on its first service — chlorine breakthrough damages TFC membranes irreversibly. Keeping the carbons fresh is the single most important thing you can do for membrane lifespan.

reverse-osmosis-ro-membrane-400-gpd-appr.description:
The **TFC-3013-400** — a 400 GPD reverse osmosis membrane element designed for commercial RO systems, high-demand residential setups, and small-business water purification installations. At 400 GPD = **1512 L/day**, this element produces roughly 5× the daily volume of a standard 75 GPD residential membrane, suiting installations where peak demand or storage-tank refill rate matters more than the smaller residential format can deliver.

## Documented Performance

Under the manufacturer's standard test conditions (65 PSI, 25 °C, 500 ppm NaCl feed, pH 6.5–7.5, 15% recovery rate):

- **Stable desalination rejection:** 97%
- **Minimum desalination rejection:** 95%
- **Mean permeable flow:** 400 GPD (1512 L/day)
- **Active film area:** 16 ft² (1.92 m²)

These are tested figures, not generic "up to 99%" marketing claims — documented at the same test conditions used across the industry.

## Operating Window

- **Maximum operating pressure:** 300 PSI (2.07 MPa)
- **Maximum feed water temperature:** 45 °C
- **Maximum feed water silt density index (SDI):** 5
- **Feed water pH range, continuous operation:** 3–10
- **Feed water pH range, short-term cleaning:** 2–12
- **Maximum pressure drop across element:** 10 PSI (0.07 MPa)

## Critical — Chlorine Tolerance

**Maximum feed water free chlorine: < 0.1 ppm.** This is the most important number on this spec sheet for installation planning. Standard Australian town water is dosed at 0.5–1.5 ppm free chlorine — already 5×15× above the membrane's tolerance. The membrane will be destroyed within weeks if installed without an effective activated carbon stage upstream to remove residual chlorine from the feed.

For any installation:

- Always run an activated carbon stage upstream of this membrane
- Replace the carbon stage on its scheduled interval (6–12 months) without exceptions — a saturated carbon stage allows chlorine breakthrough that destroys the membrane downstream
- Test the feed pre-membrane periodically with a free-chlorine test kit if you're running on highly chlorinated supply

Not a residential drop-in for under-sink systems — the 3013 housing is significantly larger than the standard 10" × 2.5" RO housing used in 4/5/6-stage residential setups.

If you're sizing a high-volume RO build from scratch, contact us before ordering — a TFC-3013-400 needs the right housing, the right pre-filter sizing for its flow rate, and a feed-water analysis to size correctly.

2x-poly-spun-water-filter-cartridge-5-mi.shortDescription: Twin pack of polypropylene spun sediment cartridges — 20" × 4.5" Big Blue, 5 micron. One year of routine sediment filtration for a whole-house system at 6-month change intervals.
2x-poly-spun-water-filter-cartridge-5-mi.description:
A twin pack of 20" × 4.5" Big Blue polypropylene spun sediment cartridges, sized for whole-house filtration on a 6-month change cycle. Two cartridges in the pack — install the first now, keep the second on the shelf for the next change-out, and you've covered roughly a year of sediment filtration without re-ordering.

The spun-melt construction means the polypropylene fibres are extruded and bonded as a single continuous structure, with no plastic centre core. That's the build difference that matters in practice: water flows through the full cross-section of the cartridge, not just the outer wall, so the cartridge holds more dirt before pressure drop forces a change.

## Why the Twin Pack

For a whole-house Big Blue filter running on Australian town water, **the sediment stage is the cartridge that hits replacement schedule first** — sediment loads it, not chemistry. Tank water and bore-fed properties go through them faster again. Buying in a pair drops the per-cartridge cost and means the spare is on the shelf the day the pressure differential or visible discolouration tells you it's time. polypropylene-sediment-water-filter-pp-5.description:
The standard 10" × 2.5" polypropylene sediment cartridge — the workhorse pre-filter that goes in Stage 1 of nearly every multi-stage residential filter sold in Australia. RO systems, under-sink twin and triple housings, bench-top filters, fridge inline kits — they all use this size and this format.

## What It Does and Why Stage 1

This is the cartridge that catches **sand, silt, rust flakes, and visible particulate** before water reaches the carbon stages or the RO membrane. That ordering matters: sediment is what physically clogs the dense carbon block downstream, and even a small amount of grit will slowly destroy the surface of an RO membrane. Spending $17 on a sediment pre-filter to protect a $60 carbon block and a $90 RO membrane is the maths that makes multi-stage filtration economic.

Rated to **5 microns**, which is the sweet spot for a Stage 1: fine enough to catch the particulate that matters for downstream protection, coarse enough to not load up and force a premature change.

## Operating Window

- **Operating temperature:** 5–40 °C
- **Operating pressure:** 0.1–0.4 MPa (14.5–58 PSI)
- **Lifespan:** 6–12 months depending on water quality and household usage

If your incoming mains pressure runs above 58 PSI — common in parts of Sydney, Melbourne, and the Central Coast — install a pressure-limiting valve upstream. Cartridges run outside their rated pressure window will fail prematurely or split internally, dumping their sediment load downstream.

## Where It Fits

Designed for any standard 10" × 2.5" filter housing — the most common size in Australian residential filtration. Same physical fit across RO systems, under-sink twin packs, bench-top filters, and the [single-stage clear sediment whole-house](/whole-house-water-filter-clear-sediment-1-stage/) housing.

For installations where the housing has the headroom but you don't want to step up to the wider 4.5" Big Blue diameter, this is the format that buys longer service intervals on the same physical housing footprint.

## Why Step Up From 10" × 2.5"

A 10" × 2.5" cartridge holds a fixed amount of polypropylene media. When that media saturates with sediment, pressure drop rises and the cartridge has to come out — typically at the 6–12 month mark on Australian town water. The 20" × 2.5" doubles the media volume in the same diameter, which means it can carry roughly twice the sediment load before reaching the same pressure-drop threshold.

In practice, that translates to fewer cartridge changes per year, lower running cost over a 5-year horizon, and less time spent on the wrench. Where it doesn't translate is flow rate: same 2.5" diameter means same maximum flow as the shorter cartridge — for higher flow, you need 4.5" Big Blue.

premium-pair-of-water-filter-cartridges-.description:
The premium twin pack — a polypropylene spun sediment cartridge paired with a coconut activated carbon block, both in the standard 10" × 2.5" format. This is the replacement set for any 2-stage under-sink filter, sized to refresh both cartridges in a single order.

## What's in the Pack

**Cartridge 1 — Polypropylene Spun Sediment, 5 micron.** The "HPF" (High Performance Filtration) construction uses polypropylene fibres that are spun and melted simultaneously, forming a single continuous structure with no internal centre core. The benefit of no centre core is that water uses the full radial cross-section of the cartridge rather than being constrained by an internal sleeve — which means higher flow at lower pressure drop, longer service life, and no plastic core to leach into the supply.

**Cartridge 2 — Coconut Activated Carbon Block (CTO).** Coconut-shell carbon is the higher-grade carbon source — the activated structure has more surface area per gram than coal-based carbons, with no detectable heavy-metal residuals from the source material. The CTO designation ("Chlorine, Taste, Odour") describes what the carbon block is engineered to remove: chlorine, chloramines, taste compounds, and odour from the supply. Block construction (vs granular) gives longer water-to-carbon contact time at the same flow rate, which is what makes it effective.

## Why Premium Over Standard

The sediment cartridge in this pack is specifically the spun-melt no-centre-core construction, and the carbon is coconut-shell rather than coal-derived. Both upgrades extend cartridge life and improve filtration performance — most noticeable on chlorinated mains supplies where the carbon stage does the heavy lifting. The [standard CTO + sediment 10" × 2.5" twin pack](/twin-pair-of-water-filter-cartridges-carbon-cto-plus-sediment-pp-10-x-2-5-5-micr/) is fine for budget replacements; this one is for the customer who wants the cartridge that will last longer and treat the water more thoroughly.

## Where It Fits

For any 10" × 2.5" 2-stage under-sink filter, including the [under-sink 2-stage sediment + carbon](/under-sink-water-filter-2-stage-sediment-carbon/) system. Also suits the first two stages of multi-stage RO systems that use the 10" × 2.5" pre-filter format.

Replace as a pair every 6–12 months. The sediment cartridge typically reaches end-of-life first on Australian town water; replacing them together keeps the service interval predictable.

## Three Things to Block — One Pack

The pair is engineered around the three contaminant categories that matter for whole-house water:

1. **Sediment, dirt, rust** — handled by the PP sediment cartridge
2. **Chemicals — chlorine, organics, taste, odour** — handled by the carbon block
3. **Giardia cysts** — reduced by the 5-micron sediment stage

That last point is what makes the 5-micron sediment rating the technically correct choice rather than a coarser pre-filter. At 5 microns, polypropylene sediment filtration reduces giardia, which historically required expensive 5-micron carbon block to do. Pulling that job into the sediment stage means the carbon stage is freed up for chemistry — chlorine, chloramines, taste, odour — at whatever micron rating suits.

## "HPF" Sediment Construction

The sediment cartridge uses **spun-melt polypropylene with no centre core** — the same "HPF" construction used in the 10" × 2.5" premium pack, scaled up to Big Blue diameter and length. The benefits scale with it: full radial water flow, smooth fibre structure that resists bacterial slime growth, and high sediment-holding capacity sized for whole-house volumes. The construction is rated for filtering cooking oil, which speaks to the chemical inertness suitable for drinking-water service.

## Carbon Block, Whole-House Scale

The carbon stage is an activated carbon block in 20" × 4.5" Big Blue format — the dense block structure and large media volume give the contact time needed to handle whole-house flow rates without breakthrough. The combination of PP sediment + carbon block + Big Blue diameter is the standard Australian whole-house specification for chlorine and sediment removal.

Replace as a pair every **6–12 months** depending on your water quality and household demand.

The reason this set sits above the standard twin pack on the shelf is what the 5-micron sediment stage does beyond particulate capture: at 5 microns, polypropylene sediment filtration **reduces giardia cysts** in the water, which historically was a job that required expensive 5-micron carbon filters specifically.

That one technical fact — that a properly-rated sediment cartridge handles giardia — is why the cartridge pairing in this set works the way it does.

## The Three Things to Block

For drinking water, the three categories of contaminant that matter are:

1. **Sediment, dirt, and rust** — physical particulate from the supply line
2. **Chemicals — chlorine, organics, taste, and odour** — handled by the carbon stage
3. **Giardia (cysts)** — handled by 5-micron sediment filtration in this pack

The 5-micron PP sediment stage in this set covers (1) and (3); the coconut CTO carbon covers (2). With giardia handled by the sediment stage, you have flexibility on the carbon micron rating since carbon's job is the chemistry, not the cysts.

## Why "HPF" Construction Matters

The sediment cartridge is built using polypropylene that is **spun and melted simultaneously**, forming a single bonded structure with **no internal centre core**. Three things follow from that construction:

- **No flow restriction:** water uses the full radial cross-section, not just the outer wall
- **No bacterial-slime growth surface:** smooth fibre structure resists biofilm
- **High sediment-holding capacity:** the cartridge runs longer between changes

It's also rated for **filtering cooking oil**, which speaks to the chemical inertness and structural integrity of the construction — a cartridge that would dissolve or shed in a cooking-oil application would be a bad pick for drinking water filtration too.

## Carbon: Coconut, Block, CTO

The carbon stage uses coconut-shell activated carbon in block format. Coconut carbon has higher surface area per gram than coal-based carbons and avoids the heavy-metal residuals that some coal sources carry. Block construction gives extended water-to-carbon contact time vs granular fills — the right format for chlorine and chloramine reduction at residential flow rates.

3-way-filtered-kitchen-tap-for-ro-water-.shortDescription: Sophisticated 3-way filtered kitchen tap — hot, cold, and RO-filtered water from a single fixture. Available in matte black, brushed gold, brushed nickel, or polished chrome. WaterMark certified, WELS 4★ at 7.5 L/min (T40393).
3-way-filtered-kitchen-tap-for-ro-water-.description:
A 3-way filtered kitchen tap that delivers hot, cold, and RO-filtered water through a single sleek fixture — available in four luxurious finishes to match any contemporary kitchen palette. The premium choice for RO installations where you don't want to drill a second tap hole.

## Four Finish Options

- **Matte Black** — high-contrast contemporary look, pairs with timber and stone benchtops
- **Brushed Gold** — warm metallic accent, suits premium and statement-piece kitchens
- **Brushed Nickel** — warm-toned, forgiving of fingerprints, neutral with most palettes
- **Polished Chrome** — bright timeless finish, works with both warm and cool colour palettes

All four finishes share the same internal mechanism, the same dimensions, and the same WaterMark + WELS certification — the choice is purely visual.

## How 3-Way Works

A single tap body routes three water sources through internal channels:

- **Hot** from the standard hot supply line
- **Cold** from the standard cold supply line
- **Filtered** from a separate RO permeate line through its own internal channel

The filtered-water channel is **physically separated** from the hot/cold pathway inside the tap — RO permeate doesn't carry chlorine, so it can't mix back with chlorinated mains water through the standard mixer cartridge. A dedicated lever or button on the tap activates the filtered output.

## Why This Solves the Second-Tap-Hole Problem

Standard RO installations require **two tap holes in the bench** — one for the kitchen mixer, one for the dedicated filter dispensing tap. On stone benchtops, single-hole sinks, or new builds with sealed splashbacks, drilling that second hole is a non-trivial job: stone fabrication, potential warranty implications, and a permanent extra fixture in the visual line.

This 3-way tap routes all three water sources through one tap body — install in your existing single bench hole, route the RO permeate to the dedicated channel, done. No drilling, no extra fixture, no second handle on the bench.

## Australian Compliance

**WaterMark certified** to **AS/NZS 3718** (Plumbing fittings — General requirements). Your licensed plumber can install this on a mains supply line and issue a certificate of compliance.

**WELS 4-star rated at 7.5 L/min** under AS/NZS 6400:2016 — the standard water-efficient rating. WELS registration number **T40393**.

## Where This Tap Fits

- Single-hole sink installations needing both standard and RO-filtered water
- New kitchen builds wanting a clean single-fixture bench
- RO system upgrades replacing separate filter taps with a unified fixture
- Premium kitchens choosing one of the four finishes as a design accent

bathroom-water-saving-round-shower-set-r.shortDescription: Complete shower set with round rainfall head, hand shower, and wall-mounted mixer — solid brass construction, water-saving design. WaterMark and WELS certified for legal mains installation.
bathroom-water-saving-round-shower-set-r.description:
A complete round shower set built around a **rainfall overhead head**, a hand shower, and an adjustable wall-mounted mixer — sized for residential bathroom installations where you want both the indulgent overhead spray and the practical handheld for cleaning, rinsing, and accessibility.

## Why a Two-Head Configuration

A fixed rainfall head alone is great for the overhead spray experience but useless for rinsing the bath after kids, cleaning the shower walls, or directing water where you actually need it. A hand shower alone is practical but doesn't give you the wide, gentle overhead spray that most people install a shower for.

A two-head set gives you both — switch via the mixer between the rainfall head and the hand shower (or in some configurations, run both together for a more enveloping shower experience).

## Build

- **Material:** brass body throughout — corrosion-resistant for long-term humid bathroom environments
- **Heads:** round rainfall overhead + round hand shower
- **Mixer:** adjustable wall-mounted single lever
- **Installation:** wall mounted
- **Finish:** silver / chrome (model 17003 in chrome/black)
- **Warranty:** 1 year manufacturer

## Compliance

**WaterMark certified** and **WELS rated** per supplier specification. Additionally certified to **CE** (European) and **cUPC** (US-Canadian plumbing) standards. Your licensed plumber can install this on a mains supply line and issue a certificate of compliance.

Under Australian plumbing regulations, only WaterMark-certified showers may be permanently plumbed into a mains supply — this product meets that requirement, so the install is legal and the home insurance position is sound.

## Pre-Install Note

Before install, flush the supply pipework to clear sediment, sand, or scale that could otherwise enter the mixer cartridge or restrict the rainfall head perforations. This is the most common cause of warranty claims on shower sets — a 30-second flush prevents it.

in-wall-dual-flush-toilet-button-facepla.shortDescription: In-wall dual-flush toilet button faceplate — circular dual-button design for concealed cisterns. ABS construction, four finish options (matte black, polished chrome, brushed gold, brushed nickel). Universal compatibility.
in-wall-dual-flush-toilet-button-facepla.description:
A **dual-flush button faceplate** for in-wall concealed cistern toilets — the visible flush-button assembly that sits on the wall face above the toilet pan, with two buttons (large for full flush, small for half flush) in a clean circular design.

## What This Replaces or Complements

In-wall concealed cistern toilet installations have two visible elements on the bathroom wall side:

1. **The toilet pan** (mounted to the floor or wall below)
2. **The flush button faceplate** (mounted on the wall above the pan, operating the cistern hidden behind the wall)

The **faceplate is the customer-visible interface** with the otherwise-invisible plumbing — it's what the user touches every day, and it's what defines the visual personality of the toilet installation.

This faceplate is the **circular design variant** — round buttons in a round surround. The contrast option to the rectangular faceplate, which uses square geometry in the same finish range.

## Four Finish Options

- **Matte Black** — high-contrast modern accent against white wall tile
- **Polished Chrome** — bright timeless finish, neutral with most palettes
- **Brushed Gold** — warm metallic, premium statement piece
- **Brushed Nickel** — warm-toned metallic, forgiving of fingerprints, neutral with most palettes

All four finishes are applied over an ABS substrate — durable, corrosion-resistant, and easy to clean.

## Dual-Flush Operation

- **Large button:** full flush (typically 4.5 L)
- **Small button:** half flush (typically 3 L)

The water-saving dual-flush system is the standard configuration for modern Australian toilets. The button design makes the selection visually intuitive — bigger button for bigger flush, smaller button for smaller flush.

## Build

- **Material:** high-quality ABS plastic — corrosion-resistant, dimensionally stable, easy to clean
- **Design:** circular dual-button
- **Operation:** smooth easy-press for comfortable use
- **Compatibility:** universal — fits a range of concealed in-wall cisterns

ABS plastic is the standard premium faceplate material — it resists staining, doesn't corrode in the wet bathroom environment, and accepts a wide range of plated finishes without surface degradation.

## Compatibility

Fits a **range of concealed in-wall cisterns** — including the [Enviro Aqua in-wall concealed cistern toilet system](/in-wall-concealed-cistern-toilet-rimless-floor-mount-pan-chrome-buttons-wels/). Confirm cistern compatibility before ordering — different cistern brands use different button-rod mechanisms.

## Where This Faceplate Fits

- Premium bathroom builds with in-wall concealed cistern toilets
- Renovations replacing an aged faceplate with a refreshed finish
- Bathrooms choosing the circular design over rectangular as a design preference
- Cistern installations needing finish coordination with other bathroom fixtures

For most contemporary residential bathrooms in Australia, rectangular faceplates are the more common choice — they pair naturally with the rectangular vanity bowls, rectangular mirrors, and tile patterns that dominate modern builds.

- **Matte Black** — high-contrast modern accent

- **Large button:** full flush (typically 4.5 L)
- **Small button:** half flush (typically 3 L)

- **Operation:** smooth easy-press for comfortable use

- Renovations replacing an aged faceplate with a refreshed finish
- Cistern installations choosing rectangular geometry over circular

rimless-watermark-back-to-wall-toilet-so.shortDescription: Rimless back-to-wall toilet suite with soft-close seat — WaterMark certified, WELS 4★ dual flush at 4.5L/3L. Modern hygienic rimless bowl, concealed plumbing, easy cleaning. Local pickup Central Coast NSW.
rimless-watermark-back-to-wall-toilet-so.description:
A back-to-wall rimless toilet suite designed for modern bathrooms — hygienic rimless bowl design, soft-close seat, WELS 4-star dual flush, and a clean back-to-wall installation that conceals the plumbing for a flush, modern look.

## What 'Rimless' Actually Means

Traditional toilets have a rim under the bowl that water flushes from — and underneath that rim, there's a hidden cavity that's almost impossible to clean. Bacteria, grime, and mineral buildup accumulate in that cavity over years, and no amount of scrubbing reaches the worst of it.

A **rimless design** does away with the under-rim cavity entirely. Water enters the bowl from a higher, exposed flow channel that you can see and clean. The result:

- **No hidden surfaces** for bacteria to colonise
- **Easier and faster cleaning** — every wettable surface is visible and accessible
- **Better long-term hygiene** without aggressive cleaning chemicals
- **Flushed appearance** that looks newer for longer

## Back-to-Wall Design

The back-to-wall design hides the plumbing connections inside the wall cavity rather than exposing them behind the bowl. The toilet sits **flush against the wall** with no visible cistern feed pipes — cleaner visual, easier cleaning around the base, and a more contemporary look than the older detached-cistern format.

## Soft-Close Seat

The soft-close seat hinge mechanism stops the lid and seat from slamming down when released. Three practical effects:

- **No noise** — the seat lowers silently regardless of how it's released
- **No damage** — slammed seats crack porcelain over time; soft-close eliminates that wear
- **No pinched fingers** — relevant in households with young children

## Water Efficiency

**WELS 4-star rated** with a **dual flush system** delivering 4.5 L full flush and 3 L half flush — well below the older 9 L/4.5 L single-flush standard, with no compromise on flushing performance.

## Dimensions and Plumbing

- **Overall:** 605 mm L × 380 mm W × 800 mm H
- **P-trap:** 180 mm centre height (the standard for wall-exit plumbing)
- **S-trap:** 100 / 250 mm centre offset (for floor-exit plumbing)

The unit suits either wall-exit or floor-exit plumbing — the trap position is configurable at install. Confirm your existing waste outlet position before purchase.

## WaterMark Certified

**WaterMark certified to AS/NZS 6400** — your licensed plumber can install this on a mains supply line and issue a certificate of compliance.

## Local Pickup

Available for **local pickup from our Central Coast NSW location** — ideal for urgent bathroom upgrades, same-day replacements, or renovations where delivery scheduling is a constraint. Contact us to confirm pickup availability before travelling.
