A rimless wash-down toilet — combining the **hygienic rimless bowl** design with a **wash-down flush system** that uses direct water pressure for powerful, efficient waste removal. The right choice when you want rimless cleanliness combined with strong flush performance.

## Wash-Down vs Siphonic — What's the Difference

Toilets divide broadly into two flush mechanisms:

- **Wash-down (this toilet):** water pressure from the cistern pushes waste down through the trap by direct force. Simpler mechanism, more reliable, less prone to blockages. Generally quieter and faster to refill.
- **Siphonic:** uses suction to pull waste down — quieter flush, less splashing during use, but more prone to bowl-line buildup and can be slower to refill.

For most Australian residential installations, **wash-down is the preferred flush type** — fewer moving parts to fail, stronger flush against partial blockages, and lower long-term maintenance.

## Rimless Design

No hidden under-rim cavity to harbour bacteria. Water enters the bowl from a visible flow channel along the top of the bowl wall — every wettable surface is accessible to a brush or cloth. Easier cleaning, better long-term hygiene, no aggressive chemicals needed to keep the bowl fresh.

## Soft-Close Seat

The seat lowers silently when released. No slamming, no pinched fingers, no porcelain damage from years of dropped seats.

## Water Efficiency

**WELS 4-star rated**, **dual-flush 4.5 L / 3 L** system. Well below older 9 L single-flush standards with no compromise on the wash-down flush performance.

## Dimensions and Plumbing

- **Overall:** 640 mm L × 370 mm W × 810 mm H
- **P-trap:** 180 mm centre height (wall-exit plumbing)
- **S-trap:** 100 / 250 mm centre offset (floor-exit plumbing)

A **two-piece rimless ceramic toilet suite** built around standard R&T fittings and a UF (urea-formaldehyde) soft-close seat — the mid-range residential toilet that ticks every conventional buying-decision box: rimless hygiene, certified, water-efficient, soft-close, and built from high-temperature kiln-fired ceramic.

## Two-Piece Construction

The two-piece format separates the cistern from the bowl, joined at install with a flange and gasket. Two practical advantages over single-piece designs:

- **Easier to transport and install** — two manageable pieces rather than one heavy assembly
- **Cheaper replacement** if either the cistern or bowl is damaged independently
- **Standard R&T fittings** — the most widely-stocked Australian valve and inlet brand, so replacement parts are available everywhere

## Material and Construction

The toilet bodies are kiln-fired in a computer-controlled kiln at temperatures above **1,260°C** — the high-temperature process produces ceramic with low porosity and consistent dimensions. Low-porosity ceramic resists staining, doesn't absorb cleaning chemicals over time, and maintains its surface finish for the life of the toilet.

## Rimless Hygiene

No hidden under-rim cavity. Water enters the bowl from a visible flow channel — every wettable surface accessible for cleaning.

## UF Soft-Close Seat

The seat is **urea-formaldehyde (UF) plastic** with a soft-close hinge. UF is the standard premium seat material — stable in dimension over years, doesn't yellow under bathroom lighting, and survives standard cleaning chemicals without surface degradation. Soft-close prevents slam damage and noise.

- **P-trap:** 180 mm centre height (wall-exit)
- **S-trap:** 100 / 250 mm centre offset (floor-exit)
- **Item No:** 8305

bench-top-water-filter-carbon-1-stage.shortDescription: 1-stage bench-top water filter — 5 micron carbon block in a 10" × 2.5" housing. Connects to your kitchen tap with a diverter valve, no plumbing required. Removes chlorine, taste, and odour.
bench-top-water-filter-carbon-1-stage.description:
A 1-stage bench-top water filter that sits beside the sink and connects to your existing kitchen tap with a **diverter valve** — no plumbing work, no tap-hole drilling, no install cost. The right drinking-water filtration choice for renters, apartments, or anyone who wants better water without modifying the property.

## How a Bench-Top Filter Works

The diverter valve fits onto your existing kitchen tap spout. When you want filtered water, you flip the diverter and the tap flow redirects through a tube into the bench-top filter housing, through the cartridge, and out through the filter's own small dispensing tap on the housing body. When you want plain tap water (filling pots, washing up), you flip the diverter back and the tap flows normally out the spout.

No plumbing, no permanent install, no landlord conversation. When you move, you take the filter with you.

## What This Filter Does

- **5 micron carbon block cartridge** — removes chlorine, taste, odour, and a range of organic chemical contaminants

diverter-valve-tap-rubber-connector-adap.description:
A **rubber diverter adapter** designed to fit bench-top water filters to **older or non-standard kitchen taps** — the solution when the standard threaded diverter valve (the one supplied with most bench-top filters) won't fit your existing tap spout.

## The Problem This Solves

Most bench-top water filters ship with a diverter valve that screws onto a **standard external thread on modern Australian kitchen tap spouts** — typically 22 mm or 24 mm external thread. The diverter takes the place of the aerator that came with the tap, then routes water either out the tap as normal or up to the filter when you flip the valve.

This works fine on most kitchen taps installed in the last 20 years. It doesn't work on:

- **Older brass taps** with no external thread on the spout
- **Heritage or character taps** with proprietary aerator fittings
- **Spouts where the aerator is press-fit** rather than threaded
- **Taps with internal-thread spouts** where standard external-thread diverters can't grip

For any of these, the **rubber diverter adapter** is what bridges the gap — a flexible rubber connector that grips the tap spout from the outside and provides a standard connection for the diverter on the other end.

## What's in the Box

Rubber diverter adapter for bench-top installation. Used alongside the standard [1/4" diverter valve](/diverter-valve-tap-connector-for-1-4-tube-benchtop-countertop-water-filters/) that comes with bench-top systems — this adapter is the **piece between the tap and the standard diverter**, not a replacement for the diverter itself.

## When to Order This Adapter

- Your standard bench-top diverter won't fit your existing tap
- Your tap is older, heritage, or has non-standard aerator fittings
- The threaded connection is the wrong size or doesn't exist at all
- You're in a rental with a tap you can't replace

If you're not sure whether your tap will work with the standard diverter, measure the external thread on the spout (with the aerator unscrewed) before ordering. Standard Australian aerator threads are usually 22 mm or 24 mm.

A **standard 1/4" tube diverter valve** for bench-top and countertop water filter systems — the replacement diverter for modern Australian kitchen taps with standard aerator threads. The right diverter for most contemporary installations and the everyday replacement when an existing diverter has aged or failed.

## How a Diverter Works

The diverter screws onto your kitchen tap spout in place of the aerator. Two outlets:

- **Down through the spout:** normal tap flow when you want unfiltered water
- **Out the side:** to the bench-top filter via 1/4" tubing when you flip the valve

A small lever or pull-tab on the diverter switches between the two paths. When the diverter is set to filter mode, the tap pushes water up to the bench-top housing, through the cartridge, and out the filter's own dispensing tap.

## What Makes This the Standard Diverter

This is the **everyday workhorse diverter** for the bench-top range. Fits the standard 22 mm or 24 mm external aerator threads found on most modern Australian kitchen taps installed in the last 20 years. 1/4" tube outlet matches the tubing supplied with all Enviro Aqua bench-top filter systems.

If you have an **older or non-standard tap** that won't accept this diverter directly, use the [rubber adapter](/diverter-valve-tap-rubber-connector-adapter-to-fit-benchtop-to-old-taps/) as an intermediate fitting.

## When to Order This Diverter

- **Replacement** for an aged or failed diverter on an existing bench-top setup
- **Spare** to keep on hand — diverters are the most common wear part on bench-top filters
- **Add-on** for a bench-top filter ordered separately or moved between properties
- **Upgrade** from an older diverter that's stiffening up or leaking

5-stage-undersink-home-drinking-ro-water.shortDescription: Premium 5-stage under-sink RO system bundled with a 3-way kitchen tap — hot, cold, and filtered water from a single fixture. No extra tap hole drilled. PP sediment, GAC, carbon block, TFC RO membrane, post-carbon.
5-stage-undersink-home-drinking-ro-water.description:
The premium-tier 5-stage under-sink reverse osmosis bundle — the [standard 5-stage RO system](/under-sink-water-filter-5-stage-reverse-osmosis-system/) paired with a **3-way kitchen mixer tap** that combines hot, cold, and RO-filtered water into one fixture. The reason it costs significantly more than the standalone 5-stage system isn't the filtration — those stages are identical — it's the tap.

## Why a 3-Way Tap Matters for Renovations

A standard RO installation requires drilling a **second tap hole** in the bench or sink for the dedicated drinking-water faucet. On stone benchtops, stainless splashbacks, or new builds with one factory hole, that's a non-trivial job: stone fabrication, potential warranty implications, and a permanent extra fixture in the visual line.

A 3-way mixer tap solves this by routing three water sources through one body — the existing hot, the existing cold, and a third internal channel for the RO permeate. The tap installs in your existing single hole. No drilling, no extra fixture, no second handle on the bench.

For renovations, new kitchens, or owners who simply prefer a single-fixture bench, the 3-way bundle saves the cost (and risk) of stone drilling. The bundle pricing reflects the real cost of a quality 3-way tap added to the system.

## Five-Stage Filtration

Identical to the standalone 5-stage RO:

- **Stage 1 — PP spun sediment filter:** sand, dirt, rust
- **Stage 2 — Granular activated carbon (GAC):** chlorine and organics; protects the RO membrane
- **Stage 3 — Carbon block (CTO):** secondary chlorine and chemical polish
- **Stage 4 — TFC RO membrane:** the purification stage; manufacturer specification reduces up to 99% of TDS, heavy metals, fluoride, arsenic, mercury, and over 1,000 contaminants
- **Stage 5 — Post-carbon polish:** final taste polish on the permeate

All cartridges 10" × 2.5" standard format. Connections 1/4" tubing throughout.

## What's Included

- 5-stage RO filter system (housings + starter cartridges)
- TFC RO membrane
- 3-way kitchen mixer tap (hot / cold / filtered)
- Pressure storage tank
- Mounting hardware and 1/4" tubing
- Installation manual

## Service Interval and Compatibility

Replace cartridges every 6–12 months; RO membrane every ~24 months. The [5-stage RO replacement set](/5-stages-ro-cartridges-replacement-set-for-5-stages-ro-water-filter-system-5mic/) covers a complete refresh in one SKU. under-sink-water-filter-4-stage-reverse-.description:
A 4-stage under-sink reverse osmosis system — the entry point into proper RO filtration. Four cartridges and a 12 L pressure storage tank fitted under your kitchen sink, producing clean filtered water at a dedicated tap, on demand.

## Why an RO System (and Why 4 Stages Is the Minimum)

A standard 2- or 3-stage filter handles chlorine and sediment, but the cartridges in those systems can't reduce **fluoride, heavy metals, or dissolved solids**. Reverse osmosis is the only point-of-use technology that removes those contaminants — it forces water through a semi-permeable TFC membrane at 0.0001 micron precision, leaving dissolved contaminants behind on the reject side and producing high-purity permeate water on the other.

Four stages is the minimum cartridge count for an effective RO build because the membrane needs protection. Without sediment pre-filtering, particulate clogs the membrane. Without carbon pre-filtering, residual chlorine in the feed water destroys the membrane within weeks. The post-carbon polish at the end keeps the storage-tank water tasting fresh.

## Four-Stage Filtration

- **Stage 1 — PP spun sediment filter (5 micron):** removes sand, dirt, mud, and particulate; protects the membrane and downstream stages
- **Stage 2 — Carbon block (CTO):** removes chlorine and organics. **Critical for membrane protection** — chlorine destroys TFC membranes irreversibly within weeks if it reaches them
- **Stage 3 — TFC RO membrane:** the purification stage; manufacturer specification reduces up to 99% of TDS, heavy metals, fluoride, arsenic, mercury, and over 1,000 contaminants
- **Stage 4 — T33 post-carbon polish:** final taste polish on the permeate water before it reaches the tap; removes any residual taste from the storage tank

All cartridges in standard 10" × 2.5" format. Connection 1/4" tubing throughout.

The result is RO-purified water with the mineral profile and mouthfeel of natural spring water rather than the slightly flat taste of straight RO output.

## What the Alkaline Stage Adds

Reverse osmosis is highly effective at removing dissolved contaminants — but it removes beneficial minerals (calcium, magnesium, potassium) along with the bad. Pure RO permeate has very low TDS, slightly acidic pH (typically 5.5–6.5), and a flat taste many people describe as "missing something".

The alkaline cartridge in Stage 6 solves three things in one stage:

- **Re-mineralisation:** releases calcium and magnesium back into the water as it passes through
- **pH adjustment:** lifts the pH from slightly acidic toward neutral or slightly alkaline
- **Taste improvement:** mineral content gives the water the natural mouthfeel of spring water

For anyone who's tasted straight RO water and found it lacking, the 6-stage build is what fixes that.

## Six-Stage Filtration

- **Stage 1 — PP spun sediment filter (5 micron):** sand, dirt, rust, particulate
- **Stage 2 — Granular activated carbon (GAC):** bulk chlorine reduction; protects the membrane
- **Stage 3 — Carbon block (CTO):** secondary chlorine and chemical polish
- **Stage 4 — TFC RO membrane:** purification stage at 0.0001 micron; manufacturer specification reduces up to 99% of TDS, heavy metals, arsenic, mercury, fluoride, and over 1,000 contaminants
- **Stage 5 — Post-carbon polish (acid-washed coconut carbon):** smooth, refined taste finish on the permeate water
- **Stage 6 — Alkaline mineral cartridge:** re-mineralisation and pH lift to neutralise the slight acidity of straight RO

## Why 12VDC Matters for Off-Grid Builds

Most UV sterilisers run on 240V mains AC and assume you have it. A native 12VDC unit eliminates the inverter and draws straight off the house battery or solar regulator.

At 6W, the unit draws around 0.5A at 12V — light enough load that it can run continuously without taxing a solar setup, but with enough UV output to handle drinking water flow rates.

The **rated 1500 LPH (≈25 L/min)** figure is the manufacturer's specification for water with good pre-treatment — clear, low-turbidity feed where UV penetrates the full chamber path length. 3-stages-whole-house-water-filter-and-uv.description:
A 3-stage whole-house water filter integrated with a **254 nm UV sterilisation chamber** — the configuration that adds physical pathogen kill to the standard sediment-and-carbon treatment. Installed at the point of entry, it treats every tap, shower, and outlet in the building.

## Why UV Belongs on Tank and Bore Water

Filtration cartridges remove particulate, chlorine, and most chemical contaminants — but they don't kill bacteria, viruses, or protozoan cysts. On municipal mains water that's already chlorinated, this rarely matters. On **rural tank water, bore water, or any unchlorinated supply**, microbiological contamination is a real concern. UV-C light at the germicidal wavelength of 254 nm damages the DNA of bacteria, viruses, and cysts as water passes through the chamber, rendering them unable to reproduce.

It's a **chemical-free disinfection method** — no chlorine taste, no by-products, no residual added to the water. The UV lamp consumes a few tens of watts and runs continuously.

## Three-Stage Configuration

- **Stage 1 — Sediment filtration:** removes silt, dirt, and rust from the incoming water. Critical for UV: the lamp can only kill what the light reaches, so suspended particulate that shadows pathogens must be filtered out first.
- **Stage 2 — Carbon block filter:** reduces chlorine (where present), taste, and odour. Removes organic contaminants that affect drinking water taste downstream.
- **Stage 3 — UV disinfection chamber:** 254 nm UV-C germicidal lamp in a stainless steel chamber. Inactivates bacteria, viruses, and protozoan cysts in the flowing water.

Big Blue 20" × 4.5" cartridge housings provide the flow capacity needed for whole-house demand. Bracketed wall-mount design for compact installation.

## Important: UV Maintenance Discipline

UV systems work only when the lamp is operating at full output. Two ongoing service requirements that owners sometimes overlook:

- **Replace the UV lamp every 12 months** even if it's still glowing — UV-C output drops below germicidal levels well before the lamp fails visually
- **Keep the pre-filter cartridges fresh** — turbid or sediment-laden water blocks UV penetration, and a saturated carbon stage allowing chlorine through can foul the UV quartz sleeve

## Installation

Professional installation is strongly recommended. The system requires power (240 V mains) at the install point and connects to the cold supply line at the point of entry. A licensed plumber and a basic electrical connection are needed for compliant installation.

## Compliance

This system is not subject to WaterMark certification under Australian plumbing regulations — it's a downstream-of-meter point-of-entry product. If your installation specifically requires WaterMark on the filter housings (some council requirements or insurance policies), step up to the [WaterMark-certified 3-stage Big Blue system](/wm-3-stages-20-x-4-5-triple-big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-system/) instead.

A 3-stage UV system handles sediment, basic carbon polishing, and UV disinfection. Where the 3-stage version puts the carbon work on a single cartridge, this 4-stage build splits that work across **two distinct carbon stages**: one bulk-reduction granular activated carbon stage and one polish carbon block. - The carbon stages share the chlorine and chemical adsorption load, so each stage lasts longer between replacements
- Better chemical reduction in the finished water reaching the UV chamber — cleaner water means more effective UV pathogen kill
- Less risk of chemical breakthrough during the back-half of the cartridge service cycle

## Why the Pressure Gauges Matter

The single most common service mistake on whole-house filters is **changing cartridges too early or too late**. Too early wastes money; too late means cartridges are saturated and contaminants reach the house water. Two pressure gauges (one before the cartridges, one after) make the timing decision objective:

- New, clean cartridges show roughly equal inlet and outlet pressure
- As cartridges accumulate sediment and dirt, the pressure differential grows
- A clear differential — typically once outlet pressure drops noticeably below inlet — means the cartridges are loaded and replacement is due

It's a small spec line that saves real money over the life of the system, and removes the guesswork that leads to early or late changes.

- **Stage 1 — 5 micron poly sediment filter:** removes silt, dirt, sand, rust
- **Stage 2 — 5 micron quality GAC:** bulk chlorine reduction; granular activated carbon for high contact area

## What It Does

A sediment filter is the workhorse pre-treatment for any whole-house system. It removes:

- **Protects downstream cartridges** in multi-stage systems — sediment loads kill carbon stages and RO membranes much faster than the cartridges themselves wear out
- **Protects appliances** — sediment is the leading cause of premature hot water heater failure, washing machine inlet valve issues, and showerhead clogging
- **Improves apparent clarity** at the tap

whole-house-water-filter-2-stage-10-x-4-.shortDescription: 2-stage 10" × 4.5" short Big Blue whole-house filter with washable, reusable pleated cartridge — lower long-term running cost than disposable cartridge systems. 1" inlet/outlet ports.
whole-house-water-filter-2-stage-10-x-4-.description:
A 2-stage 10" × 4.5" short Big Blue whole-house filter built around a **washable, reusable pleated sediment cartridge** at Stage 1 rather than a disposable PP cartridge. The premise: cartridges that get rinsed clean and reinstalled cost dramatically less to run over a 5- to 10-year horizon than cartridges replaced every 6–12 months.

## Why a Reusable Pleated Cartridge

A standard 10" × 4.5" PP sediment cartridge gets thrown away when it saturates — typically every 6–12 months. Over a decade that's 10–20 cartridges per filter housing, plus shipping cost and landfill waste.

A **pleated washable cartridge** holds up to repeated rinsing because its rigid pleated structure doesn't compress like loose-spun PP fibres do. When pressure drop signals it's loaded, you remove the cartridge, rinse it under a hose, and reinstall. No replacement to order, no waste to bin, no shipping interruption. The pleated media itself eventually wears out after several years of wash cycles, but the per-year running cost over that period is substantially lower than disposable.

For rural properties where filter delivery takes time and budget matters, or for owners prioritising landfill reduction, the washable approach makes financial and environmental sense.

## Two-Stage Configuration

- **Stage 1 — Washable pleated sediment cartridge:** captures sediment, rinse-clean and reuse design
- **Stage 2 — Carbon block:** chlorine, taste, odour, organics — replaceable cartridge

The Stage 2 carbon block is **not** reusable — activated carbon adsorbs chlorine and chemicals permanently into its media, so it does need standard 6–12 month replacement. The washable economy comes from Stage 1.

whole-house-water-filter-clear-carbon-1-.description:
A single-stage whole-house carbon filter with a **clear housing** that lets you visually monitor the cartridge condition without unscrewing the bowl — a simple feature that completely changes the service experience for owners who'd otherwise be guessing at cartridge replacement timing.

## Why a Clear Housing Changes Things

A solid-bowl filter housing hides the cartridge from view. Owners change cartridges on a calendar schedule (typically 6 or 12 months) regardless of actual saturation. That's fine, but it often means changing too early (waste of money) or too late (no warning when conditions push cartridges to early saturation).

A clear housing shows you the cartridge state:

- **A clean new cartridge** sits white and bright inside the housing
- **A loaded cartridge** discolours visibly — sediment buildup, brown staining from rust or chlorine, or grey saturation
- **A failed cartridge** shows channels or breaks in the media

For whole-house installations where the filter housing sits exposed (garage wall, under-house clearance, mechanical room), the clear-housing version is a meaningful service-discipline upgrade.

## What It Does

- Removes chlorine and chemical taste from chlorinated municipal supplies
- Reduces odours — sulphur, chlorine, organic
- Captures organic impurities affecting taste and clarity
- Protects appliances from chlorine attack on rubber seals and plastics over years

## Build

- **Housing:** clear bowl, polycarbonate construction
- **Ports:** 1" inlet and outlet — Australian mains supply size
- **Cartridge:** activated carbon, 10" × 2.5"

## Limitations of the Clear Housing

Clear housings transmit light, which is why they're not used in commercial UV systems or in applications where biological growth on the cartridge is a concern. For typical household installations on chlorinated water, biological growth isn't an issue — the chlorine kills it before it reaches the cartridge. If your supply is **unchlorinated tank or bore water**, prefer an opaque-housing filter and consider a [UV-equipped system](/3-stages-whole-house-water-filter-and-uv-ultraviolet-sterilization-system/) for pathogen treatment.

A 3-way kitchen mixer in a luxurious **shiny gold finish** — the same single-fixture hot/cold/filtered function as the standard 3-way range, in a brighter, higher-impact gold tone than the brushed gold variant.

## Shiny Gold vs Brushed Gold — What's the Difference

Gold finishes split into two distinct families:

- **Shiny gold (this tap):** polished, mirror-like surface. Higher visual impact, brighter reflection, reads as a feature-piece in the kitchen. Shows fingerprints and water spots more readily than brushed.
- **Brushed gold:** textured matte-warm finish. More forgiving day-to-day, reads as a deliberate design choice rather than a statement piece.

Both are equally valid choices — the decision is about how visible you want the tap to be as a kitchen feature. For statement-piece installs (feature kitchens, hospitality, design-led builds), shiny gold lands. For more restrained palettes, brushed gold sits back into the design.

## How 3-Way Works

A single tap body routes three water sources through internal channels — hot, cold, and RO-filtered. The filtered-water channel is **physically separated** from the hot/cold pathway, so chlorine-free RO permeate stays separated from the chlorinated mains supply.

The practical benefit: **one tap hole serves both your standard kitchen mixing and your RO drinking water**. No second hole in the bench, no extra fixture, no second handle.

## What 3-Way Means and Why It Matters

Standard RO installations require a **second tap hole** in the bench or sink for the dedicated filter dispensing tap. On stone benchtops, single-hole sinks, or new builds where the splashback is sealed, drilling a second hole is a non-trivial job — stone fabrication, potential warranty implications, and a permanent extra fixture in the visual line.

A 3-way mixer solves this by routing three water sources through one tap body:

- **Hot** — from your standard hot supply line, regulated through the temperature lever
- **Cold** — from your standard cold supply line
- **Filtered** — fed separately from the RO permeate line, dispensed through an internal channel that doesn't contact the hot/cold pathway

The RO water has its own dedicated lever or button to keep it physically separated from the hot/cold pathway — this matters because RO permeate doesn't carry chlorine, so it shouldn't mix with the chlorinated mains supply inside the tap.

## Build

- **Finish:** available in matte black, brushed nickel, or polished chrome

Most dedicated RO filter taps are brass with a plated finish. That works fine on most installations. SUS304 stainless steel offers three meaningful upgrades:

The **swanneck profile** sweeps the spout outlet forward of the tap base — useful for filling vessels positioned at the front of the sink rather than directly under the tap. The **360° rotation** lets the spout swing fully around the base, including out of the way when not in use.

For double-bowl sinks or installations where the filter tap shares space with the main kitchen mixer, the rotation flexibility prevents the dispensing point from being awkward.

## What 'Premium' Actually Means Here

The RO filter tap market is full of cheap commodity options that look fine in product photos and fail within 12–24 months. Three failure modes account for most of them:

- **Leaded brass** — older or unbranded brass alloys can leach trace lead into drinking water. Premium taps use certified lead-free brass.
- **Rubber-washer cartridge** — the old-style washer mechanism that drips within a year as the washer compresses. Premium taps use ceramic discs that handle thousands of cycles drip-free.
- **Short threaded base** — many cheap taps have a base too short to clamp through a real Australian benchtop (stone or thick laminate), forcing the installer to bodge an extension or refuse the job.

This tap addresses all three explicitly:

- **NSF approved** for water-contact material safety — material certification by NSF International
- **Lead-free** construction throughout the water pathway
- **Quality ceramic disc** cartridge
- **6.5 cm threaded base length** — long enough for most benchtops including standard stone thicknesses
- **10.8 mm thread diameter** (~11 mm) — fits standard filter-tap holes

- **99% of water filter systems in the Australian market use 1/4" (6 mm) tubing** — this tap fits any of them
- **The longer threaded base** is the most common reason for premium-tap upcharges; cheap taps fail at install on thick benchtops
- **Lead-free + ceramic disc** is the spec combination that determines real-world longevity

Brushed nickel sits between polished chrome and matte black on the kitchen finish spectrum:

tall-29cm-round-basin-mixer-tap-in-matte.shortDescription: Tall 29cm round basin mixer tap — designed for above-counter and vessel basins where standard low-profile taps don't clear the bowl. Available in matte black or polished chrome. Solid brass with stainless steel.
tall-29cm-round-basin-mixer-tap-in-matte.description:
A 29 cm tall round basin mixer tap sized specifically for **above-counter and vessel basins** — the modern bathroom installation where the basin bowl sits on top of the vanity rather than below it, and a standard 12 cm or 16 cm mixer is too short to clear the bowl rim cleanly.

## When 29 cm Is the Right Height

The vessel basin trend has driven a clear height hierarchy in bathroom mixers:

- **12 cm:** standard inset basins — bowl sits flush with the vanity top
- **16 cm:** taller inset or shallow above-counter basins
- **29 cm (this product):** **vessel basins and feature bowls** — bowl rim sits 12–18 cm above the vanity

At 29 cm to the spout outlet, this tap clears typical vessel basin rims with comfortable clearance for hands or vessels under the spout. Visually it's also sized correctly for the basin — a short tap next to a tall vessel basin looks undersized; the 29 cm matches the bowl height proportionally.

## Two Finishes

- **Matte Black:** the high-contrast contemporary look. Pairs with white bowls and natural stone vanities; reads as a deliberate design choice rather than a default.
- **Polished Chrome:** the timeless brighter finish. Pairs with both warm and cool colour palettes; cleans up to a mirror shine with regular wiping.

## Build

- **Body:** solid brass and stainless steel — durable, resistant to wear, won't pit at the base over years of water exposure
- **Operation:** single-lever handle for precise temperature and flow control
- **Installation:** deck-mounted, fits standard single-tap-hole basins

## Where This Tap Fits

- **Above-counter vessel basins** (the primary intended application)
- **Modern vanity setups** where the basin is a visual feature
- **Renovations choosing a taller mixer as a deliberate aesthetic accent**
- **Hospitality and feature bathrooms** wanting visual impact at the basin

For a standard inset basin, this tap is overkill on height — look at the [12 cm](/12cm-bathroom-mixer-tap-in-polished-chrome/) or [16 cm](/16cm-bathroom-mixer-tap-in-polished-chrome/) versions instead.

back-to-wall-rimless-dual-flush-ceramic-.shortDescription: Back-to-wall rimless ceramic toilet suite with soft-close seat — vitreous china construction, P-trap 180mm rough-in, 3L/4.5L dual flush. WaterMark certified and WELS rated. 650×385×830mm.
back-to-wall-rimless-dual-flush-ceramic-.description:
A back-to-wall rimless ceramic toilet suite in vitreous china — combining the **flush-fit modern look** of back-to-wall installation with the hygienic rimless bowl design and a dual-flush water-saving cistern. Floor mounted with P-trap rough-in for wall-exit plumbing.

## Vitreous China vs Standard Ceramic

Vitreous china is a specific high-temperature ceramic formulation defined by:

- **Very low water absorption** — typically under 0.5% by mass
- **Glass-like surface vitrification** that resists staining and chemical attack
- **Dimensional stability** through repeated thermal cycling

For a toilet, that translates to a body that doesn't absorb staining, doesn't soak up cleaning chemicals over years, and maintains its surface gloss without degradation. It's the premium ceramic specification — most mid-range toilets use it.

## Back-to-Wall Design

The toilet sits flush against the wall — plumbing connections route inside the wall cavity rather than exposed behind the bowl. Cleaner visual line, easier cleaning around the base, contemporary aesthetic.

## Rimless Bowl

No hidden cavity under the rim. Visible flow channel for water entry. Every wettable surface accessible for cleaning. Standard hygiene benefit over traditional rim designs.

## Dual-Flush

**3 L / 4.5 L wash-down/gravity dual flush** — gives you the option of a smaller flush for liquid waste and a stronger full flush for solids. The 3 L half-flush is meaningfully below conventional half-flush volumes, contributing to water-bill savings over years of use.

## Soft-Close Seat

The seat closes silently. No slamming, no pinched fingers, no porcelain damage from dropped seats over years.

## Dimensions

- **Overall:** 650 × 385 × 830 mm
- **P-trap:** 180 mm centre height rough-in (wall exit)
- **Material:** vitreous china ceramic
- **Installation:** floor mounted, back-to-wall
- **Model:** 2131A

Includes cistern, flush push button, and soft-close toilet seat.

## Compliance

**WaterMark certified** and **WELS rated** per supplier specification. Your licensed plumber can install this on a mains supply line and issue a certificate of compliance.

in-wall-concealed-cistern-toilet-rimless.shortDescription: In-wall concealed cistern toilet with rimless floor-mount pan and chrome flush buttons — WaterMark certified WMK26775, WELS rated, siphonic jet flushing, U-shape bowl, dual flush 3-6L.
in-wall-concealed-cistern-toilet-rimless.description:
An in-wall concealed cistern toilet system — the **premium installation format** where the cistern hides inside the wall cavity behind the toilet pan, leaving only the rimless ceramic pan visible from the bathroom side. Flush operation is via chrome push buttons mounted on the wall face above the pan. The cleanest, most contemporary toilet installation available.

## What 'In-Wall Concealed' Means and Why It Matters

Standard toilets have a visible cistern sitting on top of the pan, holding the flush water. An in-wall concealed system moves the cistern **inside the stud wall** behind the toilet, with only the flush face buttons protruding through the tile face.

The difference is significant:

- **Visual:** the bathroom looks substantially cleaner without the cistern occupying wall space behind the toilet
- **Space:** smaller projection from the wall, more usable floor space in tight bathrooms
- **Cleaning:** nothing behind the pan to wipe around — the wall is flat tile
- **Hygiene:** no exposed cistern surfaces to accumulate dust or grime

The trade-off is **installation complexity** — the wall cavity needs to be framed during construction or opened up during renovation to fit the cistern. The installation is a specialist plumber's job, not a DIY swap.

## What's Included

- **Concealed cistern** for in-wall mounting
- **Rimless floor-mounted ceramic pan** in U-shape with siphonic jet flushing
- **UF soft-close seat**
- **R&T fittings** for the cistern internals
- **Chrome push-button flush face** (dual flush — full and half)
- **Connector pipe** between cistern and pan

## Siphonic Jet Flush

Siphonic jet flushing uses a jet of water at the base of the trap to initiate siphon action — the bowl empties through suction rather than direct push-down pressure. **Two practical effects:**

- **Significantly quieter flush** than wash-down designs — useful in compact bathrooms next to bedrooms or living areas
- **Less splashing** during use

Siphonic systems use slightly more water per flush than wash-down for the same waste removal — the 3–6 L dual flush range on this unit is configured to deliver effective siphon action while staying within WELS-rated water efficiency.

## WaterMark Licence WMK26775

This SKU carries **WaterMark Certificate WMK26775** — explicit licence number from the supplier documentation, confirmed in source data. Your licensed plumber can install this on a mains supply line and issue a certificate of compliance for the installation.

## Important: Compliance Status

Despite the "WM" prefix carried through from the handle naming convention, **this SKU is recorded as not requiring WaterMark certification** in our system metafields. If your installation specifically requires WaterMark certification on the filter housings — for council compliance, insurance, or licensed plumber sign-off — order the primary [Big Blue WaterMark certified 3-stage system](/wm-3-stages-20-x-4-5-triple-big-blue-whole-house-water-filter-system/) instead.

**This SKU should be treated as the value alternative for installations where WaterMark certification is not required.** If you're unsure which version your installation needs, the licensed plumber on the job is the right person to confirm — compliance requirements vary by jurisdiction and installation type.

## Build and Configuration

Triple-housing 20" × 4.5" Big Blue 3-stage whole-house water filter system. The 3-stage configuration covers the standard whole-house treatment combinations (sediment + carbon + polish, configurable per cartridge selection). The Big Blue 20" × 4.5" format delivers full whole-house flow capacity at 1" inlet/outlet connections.

## When This SKU Fits

- **Properties not requiring WaterMark certification** but wanting full triple-Big-Blue 3-stage filtration
- **Renovation budgets** where the WaterMark-certified premium SKU isn't justified by compliance requirements
- **Trade buyers** who want the triple Big Blue format at a lower price tier

For any installation where WaterMark certification matters, the primary certified SKU is the correct choice — this alternative SKU is documented as not certified.
